title: Predictive Buffering and FairBurst Policy for Dedicated Capacity (PRD)
creator: Maya Patel
description: High-level product requirements for adding a predictive buffering layer and a FairBurst policy to Redwood Dedicated. The goal is to reduce tail latency and failed bursts for tenants while improving overall utilization by combining short-term traffic forecasting, a small adjustable buffer of reserved slots, and an epoch-based fair-burst credit system. This PRD documents goals, user stories, acceptance criteria, constraints, and rollout plan.
background: Customers on Dedicated ask for stronger burst protection without over-provisioning reserved pools. Current approaches are static minimum reservations or aggressive short-term prewarming which either wastes capacity or still leaves tenants exposed to spikes. Engineering has prototypes for short-horizon request forecasting and a credits-based gating mechanism. This PRD consolidates product decisions and defines the operational controls and observable signals required for safe rollout.
problem_statement:
- Tenants experience transient request spikes that exceed their reserved pools and lead to elevated latencies or 429s.
- Dedicated clusters either underutilize capacity when we over-reserve for bursts, or risk SLA violations when bursts occur.
- Ops lacks precise knobs to balance utilization and fairness across tenants during short spikes.
goals:
- Reduce 95th/99th percentile latency and 5xx/429 errors during short (seconds-to-minutes) spikes for tenants on Dedicated.
- Improve utilization by avoiding large static over-reservations.
- Provide transparent controls: per-tenant buffer size, FairBurst credit policy, and observable metrics for forecasting accuracy and burst handling.
- Ensure predictable degradation: graceful eviction, prewarm hints, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants when needed.
non_goals:
- Replacing long-term autoscaling and committed capacity billing models.
- Handling extreme multi-hour traffic storms (this PRD focuses on short-horizon bursts).
- Implementing model-specific kernel changes — integration will use existing runtime APIs.
success_metrics:
- 30% reduction in tenant 99th percentile token latency during bursts (measured across pilot tenants).
- 60% fewer burst-induced 429/5xx errors for tenants enrolled in pilot compared to control group.
- No more than 5% reduction in average cluster utilization after buffers enabled.
- Forecasting MAE (mean absolute error) for short-horizon (0-120s) request rate under 15% for pilot workloads.
user_stories:
- As an SRE for a tenant, I want a small configurable burst buffer so short spikes will be absorbed without manual capacity purchases.
- As a product manager, I want to see a per-tenant forecast accuracy metric and recent burst events so I can evaluate whether to expand buffers.
- As an operator, I want an epoch-based FairBurst credit view so I can audit which tenants consumed burst capacity and why.
- As a Redwood engineer, I want automated graceful eviction and prewarm hints so rollouts remain predictable under pressure.
functional_requirements:
1) Short-term forecasting service: exposes per-tenant forecast for 0-120s horizon at 10s granularity.
2) Predictive buffer allocator: allocates small, adjustable buffer per tenant (configurable absolute slots or percentage of peak) consumed ahead of autoscale.
3) FairBurst policy engine: epoch-based credit allocation (default epoch=10 min) with overflow handling and tenant scoring to ensure no tenant monopolizes burst pool.
4) Console controls: toggle predictive buffering, configure default buffer policies, set per-tenant overrides, and view forecast accuracy.
5) Runtime integration: buffer tokens should be consumable by the serving runtime with priority over cold non-buffered requests and below reserved committed capacity.
6) Telemetry: expose metrics (forecast_mae, buffer_fill_rate, burst_credits_used, burst_evicts, 429_during_burst) and tracing hooks to link to request IDs.
7) Fallbacks: automatic downgrade to pre-configured model variants or region fallback when sustained capacity shortfall persists beyond epoch windows.
8) Admin APIs: report-only and enforced modes for initial rollout.
9) Audit logs: record credit transfers, forced evictions, and buffer overrides for compliance reviews.
nonfunctional_requirements:
- Forecasting service must respond within 50ms P95.
- Buffer accounting and credit checks must add <2ms median overhead to request admission path.
- All new telemetry must be ingestible by existing Console pipelines without schema overhaul.
- Design for eventual multi-region coordination but prototype per-region only.
- Security: change log must be captured and access controlled via existing RBAC roles.
scope_changes:
- IN SCOPE: per-tenant predictive buffers, FairBurst epoch credits, console controls, telemetry, and runtime admission integration in the hosted Dedicated runtime.
- OUT OF SCOPE: committed billing model changes, long-term autoscale algorithm rework, and on-prem private deployment parity (private parity planned later).
- POTENTIAL FUTURE: adaptive buffer sizing using per-tenant cost-utility models and ML-based anomaly detection for burst classification.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Forecasting endpoint provides per-tenant forecasts and meets latency SLA in pre-prod.
2) Predictive buffer allocations honor per-tenant overrides and default policies; buffer consumption shows expected behavior in canary tests.
3) FairBurst credit accounting enforces epoch limits and produces audit logs for each credit debit.
4) Console shows forecast accuracy, current buffer usage, burst credit balance, and recent burst events for enrolled tenants.
5) Pilot tenants (at least 3 customers, varying workload shapes) demonstrate >=30% P99 latency improvement during 90th percentile burst events versus baseline.
6) No regression in control-plane error budgets; cluster utilization drop <=5% after buffers enabled.
7) Rollback path: system can be reverted to report-only mode within 10 minutes and to pre-feature state within one deployment cycle without data loss.
8) Security review completed and audit log retention validated for compliance tenants.
rollout_plan:
1) Build instrumentation and forecasting service in staging; validate against replayed production traces.
2) Launch feature in report-only mode for all Dedicated tenants for 2 weeks to gather metrics.
3) Enable enforced mode for internal pilot tenants (3 pilot customers) with conservative default buffers and epoch settings.
4) Iterate on buffer defaults for 2 sprints, then expand to opt-in external customers.
5) After meeting success metrics, enable as optional default for all new Dedicated customers; provide migration guidance for existing reservations.
6) Post-launch: monitor telemetry for 6 weeks and run a formal reliability review before enabling automated buffer autosizing.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Forecasting inaccuracies cause wasted prewarm capacity -> Mitigation: start in report-only mode and tune thresholds; cap max buffer to small percentage of tenant commit.
- Risk: FairBurst policies are gamed by noisy tenants -> Mitigation: use smoothing windows and audits, integrate tenant scoring and manual overrides.
- Risk: Telemetry surge creates observability load -> Mitigation: sample forecasts and roll metrics pipeline updates in parallel.
- Risk: Customer confusion about billing -> Mitigation: clear Console messaging and billing FAQ; no billing changes in initial release.
open_questions:
- What should default epoch length be for different tenant classes (P0 vs P3)?
- Should buffer be charged against committed capacity or billed as transient usage? (billing decision out of scope for initial rollout)
- How to map credits to multi-model workloads with heterogeneous token costs?
- What operator thresholds trigger automated global backfill vs tenant-level eviction?
